deck_name: Murakami — ドライブ・マイ・カー Vocabulary
source: 村上春樹「ドライブ・マイ・カー」(『女のいない男たち』収録)
notes: Vocabulary drawn from Haruki Murakami's 'Drive My Car'. Optimised for an N3 learner who struggles with kanji reading. Each card includes: priority (high/medium/low) for study order, difficulty relative to N3, a simpler synonym where one exists, a short example sentence with full reading, and a kanji difficulty rating separate from JLPT level. New words added in v2 include high-frequency Murakami prose vocabulary (ふと, かすかに, etc.) that N3 learners often miss.

priority_guide.high: Learn first — blocks comprehension of key scenes if unknown.
priority_guide.medium: Learn after high priority — enriches understanding but context helps.
priority_guide.low: Passive recognition is enough — look up once, don't drill.

difficulty_guide.one_above: N2 territory — challenging but worth the effort.
difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 territory — ambitious, but these appear in the text.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common and readable even at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may be unfamiliar — learn the reading carefully.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Kanji are obscure or complex — focus on the kana reading first.

cards.simpler_synonym: 突然（でも、もっと静かなニュアンス）
cards.context: Appears constantly in Murakami prose to introduce a thought or memory that arises unbidden. Missing this word makes whole sentences feel disconnected.
cards.example_sentence: ふと彼女のことを思い出した。
cards.example_reading: ふと かのじょのことを おもいだした。
cards.example_meaning: He suddenly found himself thinking of her.

cards.simpler_synonym: 少し（でも、もっと弱いニュアンス）
cards.context: Murakami's favourite adverb for sensory detail — a faint smell, a barely audible sound. Very characteristic of his style.
cards.example_sentence: 車の中にかすかに煙草のにおいがした。
cards.example_reading: くるまのなかに かすかに たばこのにおいがした。
cards.example_meaning: There was the faint smell of cigarettes in the car.

meanings: to pose a question (to oneself or another)
cards.simpler_synonym: 聞く（でも、内省的なニュアンス）
cards.context: Kafuku's internal narration often uses this — he poses questions to himself that he cannot answer. Key to understanding his voice.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は自分自身に問いかけた。
cards.example_reading: かれは じぶんじしんに といかけた。
cards.example_meaning: He put the question to himself.

cards.context: The emotional goal of the story — can Kafuku accept what his wife was? The arc hinges on this word.
cards.example_sentence: 彼はその事実をなかなか受け入れられなかった。
cards.example_reading: かれは そのじじつを なかなか うけいれられなかった。
cards.example_meaning: He just couldn't bring himself to accept that fact.

cards.context: Murakami's characters use this when they clarify or re-frame a thought. Signals a logical turn — missing it makes reasoning feel abrupt.
cards.example_sentence: つまり、彼女は最初から知っていたということだ。
cards.example_reading: つまり、かのじょは さいしょから しっていたということだ。
cards.example_meaning: In other words, she had known from the very beginning.

cards.simpler_synonym: つまり（よりフォーマル）
cards.context: Slightly more formal than つまり — used when a character draws a conclusion after a period of reflection.
cards.example_sentence: 要するに、彼は何も分かっていなかったのだ。
cards.example_reading: ようするに、かれは なにも わかっていなかったのだ。
cards.example_meaning: In short, he hadn't understood anything at all.

cards.simpler_synonym: 分かる（でも、突然気がつくニュアンス）
cards.context: Kafuku is always noticing things — often too late. Appears frequently in key realisations about his wife.
cards.example_sentence: 彼はそのことにずっと後になって気づいた。
cards.example_reading: かれは そのことに ずっとあとになって きづいた。
cards.example_meaning: He didn't realise it until much later.

cards.context: Kafuku's profession.
cards.example_sentence: 家福は舞台俳優として有名だった。
cards.example_reading: かふくは ぶたいはいゆうとして ゆうめいだった。
cards.example_meaning: Kafuku was well known as a stage actor.

cards.context: The professional world Kafuku inhabits.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は長年、舞台に立ってきた。
cards.example_reading: かれは ながねん、ぶたいに たってきた。
cards.example_meaning: He had been on stage for many years.

cards.context: Kafuku memorises his lines by having them read aloud on tape during drives. The kanji 台詞 are hard — the reading せりふ is the important thing to learn.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は車の中で台詞を覚えた。
cards.example_reading: かれは くるまのなかで せりふを おぼえた。
cards.example_meaning: He memorised his lines in the car.

cards.context: Used specifically for traditional arts (theater, martial arts, music) rather than general practice.
cards.example_sentence: 毎日稽古があるので、彼はいつも疲れていた。
cards.example_reading: まいにち けいこがあるので、かれは いつも つかれていた。
cards.example_meaning: He was always tired because he had rehearsal every day.

cards.context: Both the craft Kafuku masters and something he suspects his wife of doing in everyday life.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女の演技は本物だったのか、それとも嘘だったのか。
cards.example_reading: かのじょの えんぎは ほんものだったのか、それとも うそだったのか。
cards.example_meaning: Was her performance real, or was it all a lie?

cards.context: What an actor inhabits — thematically mirrors the 'roles' people play in relationships.
cards.example_sentence: 彼はその役柄に深く入り込んだ。
cards.example_reading: かれは その やくがらに ふかく はいりこんだ。
cards.example_meaning: He sank deeply into the role.

cards.context: The written text of a play.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は脚本を何度も読み返した。
cards.example_reading: かれは きゃくほんを なんども よみかえした。
cards.example_meaning: He read through the script over and over.

cards.context: Kafuku's wife recorded his lines on cassette. He continues the habit with Misaki driving — the car as rehearsal space is central to the story.
cards.example_sentence: 妻が台詞を朗読したテープが残っていた。
cards.example_reading: つまが せりふを ろうどくした テープが のこっていた。
cards.example_meaning: A tape of his wife reading his lines aloud was still there.

cards.context: Chekhov's Uncle Vanya (ワーニャ伯父さん) is the specific play at the heart of Kafuku's work.
cards.example_sentence: 彼はチェーホフの戯曲を演じることが多かった。
cards.example_reading: かれは チェーホフの ぎきょくを えんじることが おおかった。
cards.example_meaning: He often performed plays by Chekhov.

cards.context: Misaki's role. The hiring of a driver frames the entire story.
cards.example_sentence: 会社は彼に専属の運転手をつけた。
cards.example_reading: かいしゃは かれに せんぞくの うんてんしゅを つけた。
cards.example_meaning: The company assigned him a dedicated driver.

cards.example_sentence: みさきは助手席に座った。
cards.example_reading: みさきは じょしゅせきに すわった。
cards.example_meaning: Misaki sat in the passenger seat.

cards.context: Where Kafuku sits and rehearses his lines.
cards.example_sentence: 家福はいつも後部座席に乗った。
cards.example_reading: かふくは いつも こうぶざせきに のった。
cards.example_meaning: Kafuku always rode in the back seat.

cards.context: Restricted vision is the reason Kafuku must hire a driver. Also works metaphorically for his emotional blind spots.
cards.example_sentence: 彼の視野は少しずつ狭くなっていた。
cards.example_reading: かれの しやは すこしずつ せまくなっていた。
cards.example_meaning: His field of vision was gradually narrowing.

cards.context: The diagnosis that leads to Kafuku's license suspension. Very specific medical term — learn the meaning, don't drill the kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 医者は緑内障の初期段階だと言った。
cards.example_reading: いしゃは りょくないしょうの しょきだんかいだと いった。
cards.example_meaning: The doctor said it was an early stage of glaucoma.

cards.context: Kafuku loses his driver's license — the plot hinge.
cards.example_sentence: 免許を取り上げられたので、運転できなくなった。
cards.example_reading: めんきょを とりあげられたので、うんてんできなくなった。
cards.example_meaning: His license was taken away, so he could no longer drive.

cards.context: The incident that triggers the eye exam and suspension.
cards.example_sentence: 駐車場で接触事故を起こした。
cards.example_reading: ちゅうしゃじょうで せっしょくじこを おこした。
cards.example_meaning: He had a minor collision in the car park.

cards.simpler_synonym: タバコ（カタカナでも書く）
cards.context: Misaki smokes with the window cracked — a small, precise detail Murakami uses to reveal her character. Note: the kanji 煙草 are rarely seen; タバコ is more common in practice.
cards.example_sentence: みさきは窓を少し開けて煙草を吸った。
cards.example_reading: みさきは まどを すこし あけて たばこを すった。
cards.example_meaning: Misaki cracked the window and smoked a cigarette.

cards.context: The governing emotion of the entire collection: 女のいない男たち — men who have lost women.
cards.example_sentence: 彼はその喪失感から立ち直れなかった。
cards.example_reading: かれは その そうしつかんから たちなおれなかった。
cards.example_meaning: He couldn't recover from that sense of loss.

cards.example_sentence: 妻が亡くなってから、彼はひどい孤独を感じた。
cards.example_reading: つまが なくなってから、かれは ひどい こどくを かんじた。
cards.example_meaning: After his wife died, he felt a terrible loneliness.

cards.simpler_synonym: 死ぬ（でも、もっと丁寧な言い方）
cards.context: Used for Kafuku's wife's death. Note: 亡くなる vs 死ぬ — both mean 'to die' but 亡くなる is more respectful and more common in narrative prose.
cards.example_sentence: 彼の妻は四十六歳で亡くなった。
cards.example_reading: かれの つまは よんじゅうろくさいで なくなった。
cards.example_meaning: His wife passed away at the age of forty-six.

cards.simpler_synonym: がん（ひらがなでも書く）
cards.context: Specifically 子宮癌 (しきゅうがん, uterine cancer) — the cause of the wife's death. The kanji 癌 is very complex; ひらがな is common.
cards.example_sentence: 妻は子宮癌で突然亡くなった。
cards.example_reading: つまは しきゅうがんで とつぜん なくなった。
cards.example_meaning: His wife suddenly passed away from uterine cancer.

cards.example_sentence: 葬儀には多くの人が集まった。
cards.example_reading: そうぎには おおくのひとが あつまった。
cards.example_meaning: Many people gathered for the funeral.

cards.context: Specific funerary term. Low priority — look up once if encountered.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は妻の遺骨を大切に持ち帰った。
cards.example_reading: かれは つまの いこつを たいせつに もちかえった。
cards.example_meaning: He carefully brought his wife's ashes home.

cards.context: Formal term — more likely to appear in written descriptions of a memorial event.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女のための追悼の言葉が読まれた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょのための ついとうのことばが よまれた。
cards.example_meaning: Words of memorial were read for her.

cards.simpler_synonym: 思い出の品（おもいでのしな）
cards.context: The cassette tapes his wife recorded are essentially 形見 — objects that carry the dead.
cards.example_sentence: そのカセットは妻の形見のようなものだった。
cards.example_reading: その カセットは つまの かたみのような ものだった。
cards.example_meaning: That cassette tape was something like a keepsake from his wife.

cards.context: The casual register for cheating. Kafuku uses this internally when trying to minimise what his wife did.
cards.example_sentence: 妻が浮気をしていたことを彼は知っていた。
cards.example_reading: つまが うわきを していたことを かれは しっていた。
cards.example_meaning: He knew that his wife had been cheating on him.

cards.context: Heavier and more moral register than 浮気 — implies sustained, serious wrongdoing.
cards.example_sentence: それは単なる浮気ではなく、不倫だったのかもしれない。
cards.example_reading: それは たんなる うわきではなく、ふりんだったのかもしれない。
cards.example_meaning: It may not have been mere cheating but a full-blown affair.

cards.context: WARNING: Not the same as English 'lover' in a romantic sense. In Japanese this almost always implies an illicit or extramarital relationship.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女には愛人がいたらしい。
cards.example_reading: かのじょには あいじんが いたらしい。
cards.example_meaning: It seems she had a lover on the side.

cards.example_sentence: 彼は妻の行為を裏切りとは呼べなかった。
cards.example_reading: かれは つまの こういを うらぎりとは よべなかった。
cards.example_meaning: He couldn't bring himself to call what his wife did a betrayal.

cards.context: The kanji 嫉妬 are notoriously hard — やきもち is the more casual alternative.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は嫉妬を感じながらも、それを認めなかった。
cards.example_reading: かれは しっとを かんじながらも、それを みとめなかった。
cards.example_meaning: He felt jealous but wouldn't admit it.

cards.simpler_synonym: 打ち明ける（うちあける）
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は死ぬ前に告白するつもりだったのかもしれない。
cards.example_reading: かのじょは しぬまえに こくはくする つもりだったのかもしれない。
cards.example_meaning: She may have intended to confess before she died.

cards.context: Kafuku's inability to let go of the unanswerable question of why his wife cheated. The story is about this 執着.
cards.example_sentence: 彼はその問いへの執着を捨てられなかった。
cards.example_reading: かれは その といへの しゅうちゃくを すてられなかった。
cards.example_meaning: He couldn't let go of his fixation on that question.

cards.simpler_synonym: 何かがおかしいという感じ
cards.context: A signature Murakami word — the subtle, pre-linguistic sense that something is off. Appears constantly in his prose.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は妻の様子にずっと違和感を覚えていた。
cards.example_reading: かれは つまの ようすに ずっと いわかんを おぼえていた。
cards.example_meaning: He had always felt something was off about his wife's behaviour.

cards.context: The long silences between Kafuku and Misaki in the car are described in detail. Murakami treats silence as a kind of speech.
cards.example_sentence: 二人は長い沈黙の中を走り続けた。
cards.example_reading: ふたりは ながい ちんもくのなかを はしりつづけた。
cards.example_meaning: The two of them kept driving through a long silence.

cards.context: Misaki's defining quality — she doesn't fill silence. Kafuku comes to trust this.
cards.example_sentence: みさきは無口だが、必要なことはきちんと言った。
cards.example_reading: みさきは むくちだが、ひつような ことは きちんと いった。
cards.example_meaning: Misaki was taciturn but said what needed to be said.

cards.simpler_synonym: 正直（でも、もっと直接的なニュアンス）
cards.context: When Misaki does speak, she is disarmingly direct — a contrast to the indirectness of Kafuku's world.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は率直に自分の意見を述べた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょは そっちょくに じぶんの いけんを のべた。
cards.example_meaning: She stated her opinion candidly.

cards.simpler_synonym: 生まれた町（うまれたまち）
cards.example_sentence: みさきは故郷の話をほとんどしなかった。
cards.example_reading: みさきは こきょうの はなしを ほとんど しなかった。
cards.example_meaning: Misaki almost never talked about her hometown.

cards.context: The industry that once sustained Misaki's dying hometown before it closed.
cards.example_sentence: その町はかつて炭鉱で栄えていた。
cards.example_reading: その まちは かつて たんこうで さかえていた。
cards.example_meaning: The town had once flourished thanks to its coal mine.

cards.context: The abandoned state of Misaki's town after the mine closed.
cards.example_sentence: 町はほぼ廃墟と化していた。
cards.example_reading: まちは ほぼ はいきょと かしていた。
cards.example_meaning: The town had nearly turned to ruins.

cards.context: How Misaki's mother died — a detail she delivers almost without emotion.
cards.example_sentence: 母親は地滑りに巻き込まれて死んだ。
cards.example_reading: ははおやは じすべりに まきこまれて しんだ。
cards.example_meaning: Her mother was caught in a landslide and died.

cards.example_sentence: これが自分の運命だと彼は思った。
cards.example_reading: これが じぶんの うんめいだと かれは おもった。
cards.example_meaning: He thought this must be his fate.

cards.context: Kafuku's memories of his wife — what is real, what was performed — are central to the story.
cards.example_sentence: 妻の記憶は少しずつ薄れていった。
cards.example_reading: つまの きおくは すこしずつ うすれていった。
cards.example_meaning: His memories of his wife faded little by little.

cards.context: Paired with 建前. Kafuku never knew his wife's 本音 — that's the wound.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女の本音は最後まで分からなかった。
cards.example_reading: かのじょの ほんねは さいごまで わからなかった。
cards.example_meaning: He never understood her true feelings, right to the end.

cards.simpler_synonym: 表向きの意見（おもてむきのいけん）
cards.context: Best learned as a pair with 本音. One of the most culturally important word pairs in Japanese.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女が見せていたのは建前に過ぎなかったのかもしれない。
cards.example_reading: かのじょが みせていたのは たてまえに すぎなかったのかもしれない。
cards.example_meaning: What she had shown him may have been nothing more than a public face.

cards.context: Does double duty — Kafuku's literal visual blind spots from glaucoma and his emotional blind spots about his wife.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女のことが彼にとってずっと盲点だった。
cards.example_reading: かのじょのことが かれにとって ずっと もうてんだった。
cards.example_meaning: She had always been a blind spot for him.

cards.example_sentence: 妻が死んでから、彼の生活には大きな空白が生まれた。
cards.example_reading: つまが しんでから、かれの せいかつには おおきな くうはくが うまれた。
cards.example_meaning: After his wife died, a vast emptiness opened up in his life.

cards.simpler_synonym: つじつまが合わないこと
cards.context: His wife loved him AND slept with other men — the contradiction Kafuku cannot resolve or let go of.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女の行動には矛盾があった。
cards.example_reading: かのじょの こうどうには むじゅんが あった。
cards.example_meaning: There was a contradiction in what she did.

cards.context: A quintessential Japanese aesthetic concept — the trailing echo of something now ended. Murakami uses it often.
cards.example_sentence: 物語が終わっても、その余韻は消えなかった。
cards.example_reading: ものがたりが おわっても、その よいんは きえなかった。
cards.example_meaning: Even after the story ended, the lingering resonance wouldn't fade.
